subject.title: Harden Program Manager behavioral evals and handoff safety

question: Should OpenClaw core accept a new scheduled Program Manager live-eval workflow that hydrates live provider/Codex secrets by default, or should this PR be narrowed to static/dispatch-only evaluation until an owner-approved live lane exists?
rationale: The diff changes a CI security boundary and adds new eval control surfaces; automation can identify the unsafe mechanics, but it should not decide whether this scheduled live-secret lane belongs in core.

options.title: Narrow Before Merge
options.body: Keep the useful contracts, static checks, telemetry helper, and tests while removing default scheduled live-secret execution until the live lane is separately approved and hardened.

options.title: Approve A Hardened Live Lane
options.body: Accept the live-eval direction only after owner approval, existing command wiring, pinned runtime images, safe env writes, and artifact-backed proof are all present.

options.title: Pause For Smaller PR
options.body: Ask for a smaller static-contract PR first and handle live workflow scheduling as a separate security-reviewed change.

recommendation.title: Narrow Before Merge
recommendation.body: Keep the useful contracts, static checks, telemetry helper, and tests while removing default scheduled live-secret execution until the live lane is separately approved and hardened.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the highest-confidence routing candidate from current-main agent/workflow history and repository ownership evidence.
